source_excerpts.text:
For a positive rational $x=p/q$ in lowest terms, define

$$h(x)=\log_2\max\{p,q\}.$$

Then

$$h(x^r)=r\,h(x),
\qquad
h(x/y)\le h(x)+h(y).$$

The height calculation in Section 2 gives, for any explicitly encoded nonnegative rational $N\times N$ matrix $Q$,

$$h(\operatorname{per}Q)
\le B_Q+\log_2(N!),$$

where $B_Q$ is its complete entry-description length.

Suppose an exact powering construction satisfies

$$\operatorname{per}(Q)=c\,\operatorname{per}(A)^r$$

with positive rational correction $c$. Necessarily,

$$\boxed{
r\,h(\operatorname{per}A)
\le B_Q+\log_2(N!)+h(c).
}$$

When $\operatorname{per}(A)\notin\{0,1\}$, its height is at least one. A superpolynomial exact power cannot therefore be hidden simultaneously in polynomial dimension, polynomial matrix bit length and polynomial correction-factor height.

This remains true if the numerical magnitude is scaled toward one: the numerator and denominator heights are still charged. The statement concerns this exact power-packing architecture. It does not exclude a different approximate representation or another permanent algorithm.
